# Z-levels
A map can have floors above and below the ground level. Each level is its own map stacked on the others. The level below shows through empty space, as in a round.
## Adding and moving
The Z-levels section of the Tools tab lists your levels. Level 0 is the ground.
- [bold]Add above[/bold] and [bold]Add below[/bold] put an empty level next to the one you're on. - Click a level in the list to go there. [bold]Up[/bold] and [bold]Down[/bold], or Page Up and Page Down, move one level. Properties has Up and Down too. - [bold]Remove[/bold] deletes your level and everything on it. It asks for a second click and can't be undone.
A session has at most 3 levels. Adding or removing levels isn't in the undo history.
Your PNG template shows only on the level you loaded it on.
## Lining up levels
Every level uses the same world tiles, and Up and Down keep you where you are, so build over what shows through from below. Every grid sits on whole world tiles at a right angle: anything placed, pasted or loaded off them, ships and maps included, moves onto them by itself. The [bold]World grid[/bold] layer draws those tiles. The [bold]Depth perspective[/bold] layer draws the levels below smaller, as on a planet; it's off by default so levels line up on screen. The Grids tab lists the grids on every level.
## Saving and downloading
Every level saves with the map. A download of a map with several levels gives one file per level, named after the map with _z and the level number, so level 0 ends in _z0.
A ship download needs exactly one grid across every level.
